diagnosed_failures: Repeated button taps stopped the action request during each new press. Confirmed intentions now stay queued; charge no longer restarts a committed first-time action.
Ordinary 20–80 ms animation scheduling could skip the fast falling-ball head-height interval. Queued aerial reception actions now search each 10 ms simulation step.

A head needed about 10–11 cm of whole-player approach while the foot-derived preparation cap was 8 cm. Headers now allow a bounded approach of at most 18 cm at 0.45 m/s across native preparation, retaining the 1 mm planning and 2.5 mm runtime skin gates.

Standing arm tracking blended too much free physics into authored poses. Active tracking residuals are smaller, and both simulation and final rendered crossfades receive independent swing/twist and collision-volume projection.
The previous arm tests only measured the hand IK target rather than the final pose. Tests now cover final elbows, shoulders and the resulting rendered forearm/trunk clearance.

The previous shirt spring logged traction but did not sufficiently resist the partner script velocity. Opposing traction now reduces actual intended locomotion; planted protection adds ground resistance.

Balance requested a sub-idle movement that the authored gait treated as standing. Corrective support now requests a stepping gait, orients the body consistently and commits the step long enough to survive an idle transition.

The legacy escape fixture tried H after F2 had re-seeded the partner outside the currently reachable arm envelope (hand gap stayed about 10.6 cm, above the unchanged 10 cm grip gate). No grip could start, so both escape assertions failed. The independent escape exercise now resets to a reachable side-on stance and starts its four-second observation after actual hand attachment. The first fixture retry had stopped H after only 2290 ms of actual grip, immediately before physical escape completed; no joint limit, grip distance or gameplay escape condition was relaxed.
Multi-call joint telemetry could interleave with simulation output. Each joint-pose row is now formatted and printed atomically.
limitations: The existing 288 procedural variants from 18 native sources are preserved. No new captured or reconstructed 3D game sequences were obtained; no claim of 100000 independently captured animations.

The balance controller remains a reduced disturbance model with authored root/leg locomotion, assisted upper body and Bullet falls. It is not a learned muscle controller or a shared 22-player articulated simulation.
Body avoidance uses approximate capsules and an elliptic trunk envelope, not a global guarantee of zero mesh-triangle intersections.
The new shirt hold and resistance tests use the scripted training partner. The full match retains native AI and tackles.

Rendered regression tests use Linux and an SDL virtual Xbox controller. Windows is crosscompiled and its portable executable/resources are verified; the Windows GUI and a physical controller were not executed here.
